children: said on Tuesday its annual profit rose 9% from a year ago, buoyed by higher crude oil prices and increased fuel sales volumes.
Sasol's headline earnings per share — a profit measure — came in at 38.31 rand ($2.38) in the year ended June 30, compared to 35.13 rand the previous year.
The company, which uses coal and natural gas to produce synthetic fuel and chemicals, said a 7% increase in the average Brent crude oil price helped propel its income.
Sasol once again skipped paying a dividend as its $3.3 billion net debt remained above the $3 billion cap in terms of its dividend policy.
